takeaways: Headings and labels describe what follows. People should know a section from its heading alone.
Put the distinguishing words first: “Billing address”, not “Address for billing”.
Avoid vague headings where clarity is needed: “Overview”, “More”, “Details”.
This one is about quality. Whether headings exist in code is 1.3.1.
failures: Buttons all labelled “Submit” for different actions
Clever headings that hide what the section contains
check: Read only the headings. Could you find what you need?
Read each label out of context. Is it still clear?
Look for identical labels that mean different things.

quiz.question: Two sections of a settings page are both headed “Options”. What does 2.4.6 ask for?
quiz.why: A heading has to describe its topic. The same heading on different content describes neither.

spec: Write final heading and label copy in the design, not placeholder text.
Flag labels that need a content review.
Where a visible label is shortened, note the full name.
review: If I read only the headings, would I know what this page does?
Which labels only make sense next to their neighbors?
Who wrote this copy, and has anyone tested it?
tradeoff: Brand voice wants personality. Navigation wants clarity. Put the voice in body copy and keep headings and labels literal.
system: Publish naming guidance with the components: verbs for buttons, nouns for headings.
pitch: Clear headings are how everyone skims. This fix helps every single user.
